hyps.why: Edge 4 (1->3) only carries signal if node 1 is fed by edge 0, so a conv there is wasted when edge 0 is none.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 can only be fed through edges 0 and 2, so a conv on edge 5 gains less than when edge 1 supplies node 2 directly.
Edge 2 (1->2) is dead when node 1 receives nothing from edge 0.
Node 2's output cannot reach node 3 when edge 5 is none, so improving edge 2 has little effect.
Edge 0's contribution reaches the output mostly via edge 4, and without it only the longer path through edges 2 and 5 remains.
Replacing none with a direct skip adds a gradient-friendly input-to-output path, whereas replacing a conv or other useful op gives little gain or a loss.
Adding a conv where there was none adds a new learnable path, while replacing an existing op yields a smaller change.
Restoring a missing edge with a strong conv helps much more than swapping from another op that already carries signal.
Reconnecting node 2 to the output with a skip gives a large gain compared with replacing an already useful op.
Removing a 3x3 conv loses more accuracy than removing an op that contributed little, such as pooling or none.
